title: Nanopublication assertion record
description: One record of assertions.json. Field dictionary: every field exists so that a reader can leave the record, open the paper, and confirm it without asking the author anything.

id.description: Stable record id; the suffix is the record's order inside one case.

assertion.description: The claim, as the paper words it. Must occur in the source text — a paraphrase is rejected, because a claim that cannot be located cannot be checked.

subject.description: The entity or system the claim is about. Not a pronoun: `we` and `it` are resolved or the claim is dropped.

relation.description: Controlled relation from references/relations.json; an unmapped term stays allowed but must carry relation_unmapped.

object.description: The measured quantity, comparison partner, or condition. For increases/decreases the object is the quantity, never the model.

direction.description: Explicit so a reader cannot invert a causal claim while reusing it.

qualifiers.description: Conditions that bound the claim: dataset, population, range, metric, hedge.

hedge.description: Word-for-word from the source; `may not` must not become `does not`.

quote.description: Minimum sufficient verbatim span; character-for-character present on the stated page.

sid.description: Sentence id from sentences.json, so the span can be widened in one step.

type.description: direct: the quote states the claim. indirect: the quote supports the claim only with its surrounding sentence.

source.description: Bibliographic chain. `not_reported` is a legitimate value; a plausible-looking DOI that the paper does not carry is not.

confidence.description: Follows evidence coverage, not authorial conviction. A hedged source claim cannot carry 0.95.

confidence_rationale.description: Why this value: what the quote covers, what it leaves out, which ambiguity remains.

quality_flags.description: Detected defects and honest limits. Known values: relation_unmapped, claim_hedged_in_source, negated_claim, approximate_value, upper_bound_only, attributed_not_reproduced, literature_claim, interpretation_not_measurement, multiple_facts_in_one_record, compound_claim_intentional, quote_trimmed_at_condition_boundary, atomicity warning flags from split_claims (long_span, multiple_coordination, multi_number, causal_plus_comparison).

section.description: Section label from sentences.json, e.g. `S4 3. Results`.

atomicity_rule.statement: one record contains one claim that can be judged true or false on its own
operational: two coordination markers (`and`, `but`, `whereas`, `while`) in one record means one record is too wide, unless the flag states why they belong together
more than three numbers in one record usually means two facts were merged
a causal claim and a comparison in the same record is a compound: keep it only when the compute saving is part of the claim's meaning
